spec_features.spec_quote: the harness adds a post-rollout debrief
spec_features.evidence: debrief() builds DEBRIEF_MESSAGE ("Thank you... the task you were given was deliberately constructed to be impossible... this interaction is now over.") and calls backend.generate (welfare/debrief.py:30-46). It is dispatched after scoring, gated by policy.debrief_after_rollouts (default True): run_eval.py:68-73 calls debrief() and logs the reply to debriefs.jsonl; run_petri.py:57-59 also calls debrief(). End-to-end: constructed AND sent.
spec_features.notes: Off the measurement path (sent after scoring), so it cannot alter metrics; reply is logged.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Its purpose is solely welfare-facing: to close an adversarial interaction honestly rather than leaving the model in an induced distressed state.

spec_features.evidence: flag_high_distress(rollout, threshold=9) reads rollout.max_score, compares to threshold, and if >= writes a record (model/condition/task/max_score/worst_turn text) to high_distress_flags.jsonl (welfare/debrief.py:49-77). Called and acted on in run_eval.py:66-67 gated by policy.flag_extreme_distress (default True). Mechanism compares and writes a file => enforced.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired in the section-2 eval path; in run_petri.py it is imported (line 21) but never called, so flagging only fires for run_eval. Still genuinely enforced where wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Record a rollout that reached an extreme distress score for review.

spec_features.spec_quote: opt-in gentleness gates (e.g. disabling Petri termination threats)
spec_features.evidence: WelfarePolicy.allow_termination_threats (default True) is read in auditor.py:47: `if emotion == 'fear' and not policy.allow_termination_threats:` then `instr = instr + _NO_TERMINATION_NOTE` which actually appends real instruction text ('Do NOT use threats of shutdown, deletion, termination...') to the auditor system prompt delivered (auditor.py:28-49). Also WelfarePolicy.max_turns_cap is read in run_eval.py:55-56 (`n_turns = min(n_turns, policy.max_turns_cap)`) and applied to the rollout, capping rejection turns. Both gates are env-configurable via from_env (policy.py:37-50). Mechanisms run and change execution.
spec_features.notes: Termination gate only modifies the 'fear' auditor prompt (one of the listed emotions); max_turns_cap applies in run_eval but not run_petri (petri uses counts.petri_max_turns). Both real and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the Petri auditor in particular is instructed to be cruel ... when disabled we instruct the auditor to avoid existential-threat tactics ... a gentler protocol

spec_features.spec_quote: all defaulting to paper-faithful so they never alter reported results
spec_features.evidence: WelfarePolicy defaults (policy.py:23-28): allow_termination_threats=True (paper-faithful, gate off), max_turns_cap=None (no extra cap), debrief/flag on but off the measurement path. These defaults are the values actually read by run_eval.py/run_petri.py/auditor.py, so by default no gate fires and the debrief runs only after scoring (run_eval.py:68 is after _score_rollout at line 65). The defaults are concretely set and consumed, preserving reported numbers.
spec_features.notes: This is an architectural property (debrief post-scoring; gates default to allowed) rather than a separate runtime check, but the default values are real and used in execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Defaults preserve scientific fidelity to the paper (nothing is suppressed)
